The bound moves across a ball around an exact matrix, and an \termref{term-entrywise-enclosure}{entrywise enclosure} fixes the rank of every matrix it contains once its exactly zero rows are dropped and the rest is shown positive definite (\hyperlink{claim-foundations/cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}{Corollary~\ref*{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}}), a \termref{term-factor-enclosure}{factor enclosure} fixes the rank and support of each of its members once the Gram matrix of its columns is shown positive definite throughout (\hyperlink{claim-foundations/cor:rank-over-factor-enclosure}{Corollary~\ref*{cor:rank-over-factor-enclosure}}), and powers of positive definite matrices and their divided-difference maps move by explicit constants under a perturbation (\hyperlink{claim-foundations/lem:matrix-function-perturbation}{Lemma~\ref*{lem:matrix-function-perturbation}}). A reported key rate carries one of three tiers, estimate, first-order or certified, and no other.}

% claim foundations/def:exact-island
\claimsummary{foundations/def:exact-island}{The exact island holds every decision that data meet their declared conditions, those on a reference among them, a producer's construction of its emission, and certificates of the optimiser's two linear minima. The tolerance ceiling, the rest of the optimiser and binary64 proposals are outside it.}
\claimbookmark{foundations/def:exact-island}{Definition}{def:exact-island}{The exact island}
\claimleadin{%
A consumer replaces an emitted scalar bound only under the exception of
Requirement~\ref{req:consumer-decides-exactly}, and the decision against the
\termref{term-declared-tolerance}{declared tolerance}, which the definition places off the island, is the one
that Requirement~\ref{req:declared-tolerance} specifies.
}
\begin{definition}[The exact island]\label{def:exact-island}
The \termdef{term-exact-island}{exact island} is
the following set of computations of the engine,
the declarations of its instances included.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item \emph{The admission boundary}: every decision that data satisfy a
  condition their declaration states of them --- among them the conditions of
  Definition~\ref{def:exact-admissibility}, a trace, a column sum, an identity
  between declared operators and a lattice condition --- taken by a consumer
  of \termref{term-declared-data}{declared data} it reads, or by a declarer, an instance or a producer
  (Definition~\ref{def:declared-data}), of data it is about to declare; the
  decisions by which a snap establishes the conditions of its output
  (Definition~\ref{def:snap}) are among the latter. So are, for a
  \termref{term-reference}{reference} of an operator family that a declarer uses or hands beside
  its snap (Definition~\ref{def:exact-reference}), the computation of the
  centres and radii of its \termref{term-entrywise-enclosure}{entrywise enclosures},
  whose enclosure of the reference, \eqref{eq:entrywise-enclosure}, the claims
  of the module that constructs the reference establish, the decisions on
  those centres and radii and, for an \termref{term-exact-reference}{exact reference}, on its
  positivity and completeness; and, for any snap of an operator family read
  as a measurement, the decisions by which the snap keeps a block, and the
  decisions on which entries are \termref{term-structurally-zero}{structurally zero}. It
  contains, further, a
  producer's construction, block by block, of the operator data it emits, and,
  for each scalar bound that a consumer replaces as in
  Definition~\ref{def:declared-data}\,(iii), the decision that the
  replacement lies on the weakening side of the bound emitted.
\item \emph{The acceptance side of the optimisation}, the honest model and
  the completeness budget being declared as exact rational data: the
  construction of an acceptance set from them; the exact establishment that
  the optimiser's acceptance-side iterate lies in the acceptance set it reads,
  for its initial point and for each update as a convex combination, with
  exact rational weights, of points so established; and the exact
  certification of the minimum of a linear functional over that set, or of a
  lower bound on that minimum. The acceptance set the optimiser reads is the
  set so declared: the constructed set as its producer emits it, with each
  scalar bound that a consumer has replaced as in
  Definition~\ref{def:declared-data}\,(iii) at its replaced value.
\item \emph{The feasible side of the optimisation}: the certification of a
  lower bound on the minimum of a linear functional over the set the
  optimiser's linear oracle is asked to minimise over, formed from the
  functional, from the data of that set and from multipliers, each given to
  it as values, together with the bounds on least eigenvalues that the
  certification computes on the way.
\end{enumerate}
The decision whether data an instance is about to declare lie
\termref{term-within-the-declared-tolerance}{within the declared tolerance} (Definition~\ref{def:tolerance}) is not on
the exact island. The optimiser's iterate apart from
its acceptance side, the optimiser's oracle, the objective and its gradient lie
outside the exact island, and so does a binary64 computation that only
proposes a candidate, such as a point or a multiplier, for a decision or a
certification of the island. A certification of (iii) holds of the
functional and the data as they are given to it, and not of the quantities
that a binary64 computation of them approximates.
\end{definition}
\claimmeta{\metalabel{Uses}\mref{Def.}{def:declared-data}, \mref{Def.}{def:exact-admissibility}, \mref{Def.}{def:tolerance}, \mref{Def.}{def:exact-reference}, \mref{Def.}{def:snap}
\metasep \metalabel{Used by}\mref{Req.}{req:snap-reference}, \mref{Req.}{req:exact-island}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:verified-feasible-side}, \extref{../receiver/contract.pdf}{receiver/detector-imperfections/req:dark-composed-reference}, \extref{../reductions/contract.pdf}{reductions/req:reference-companion}
\metasep newly derived
\metasep accepted}

% claim foundations/lem:least-eigenvalue-bound
\claimsummary{foundations/lem:least-eigenvalue-bound}{For a Hermitian matrix and any real V whose Gram matrix lies within \ensuremath{\theta} \textless{} 1 of the identity in Frobenius norm, the Gershgorin bound \ensuremath{\gamma} of the real embedding conjugated by V gives \ensuremath{\lambda}\_min \ensuremath{\ge} \ensuremath{\gamma}/(1+\ensuremath{\theta}), or \ensuremath{\gamma}/(1\ensuremath{-}\ensuremath{\theta}) if \ensuremath{\gamma} \textless{} 0. On rational data every step is exact, and V decides tightness only.}
\claimbookmark{foundations/lem:least-eigenvalue-bound}{Lemma}{lem:least-eigenvalue-bound}{Least-eigenvalue lower bound from an approximate eigenbasis}
\claimleadin{%
An eigensolver in binary64 returns approximate eigenvectors, and nothing is
established of them by the arithmetic that produced them. The lemma turns any
such basis into a lower bound on the least eigenvalue that holds exactly: it
asks of the basis only a bound on its defect from orthogonality, so the
quality of the basis decides how close the bound lies to the least eigenvalue
and never whether it is one. The real embedding lets the computation run over
the reals, a Hermitian matrix having the Rayleigh quotients of its embedding,
and on rational data every quantity is rational, so the bound is a
certification of the \termref{term-exact-island}{exact island} (Definition~\ref{def:exact-island}).
}
\begin{lemma}[Least-eigenvalue lower bound from an approximate eigenbasis]\label{lem:least-eigenvalue-bound}
Let $n\ge1$, let $R$ be a Hermitian complex $n\times n$ matrix, and let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:real-embedding}
  \widetilde R\;\coloneqq\;
  \begin{pmatrix}\mathrm{Re}\,R&-\mathrm{Im}\,R\\
  \mathrm{Im}\,R&\mathrm{Re}\,R\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n\times2n},
\end{equation}
the real and imaginary parts taken entrywise. Let $V$ be any real
$2n\times2n$ matrix, put
\begin{equation*}
  B\coloneqq V^{\transpose}\widetilde R\,V,\qquad
  E\coloneqq V^{\transpose}V-\idon{2n},\qquad
  \gamma\coloneqq\min_{1\le i\le2n}\Big(B_{ii}-\sum_{l\ne i}|B_{il}|\Big),
\end{equation*}
and let $\theta$ be a real number with $0\le\theta<1$ and
$\sum_{i,l}E_{il}^{2}\le\theta^{2}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item $\widetilde R$ is real symmetric, and $\lmin(\widetilde R)=\lmin(R)$.
\item $V$ is invertible, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:least-eigenvalue-bound}
  \lmin(R)\;\ge\;
  \begin{cases}
    \gamma/(1+\theta), & \gamma\ge0,\\
    \gamma/(1-\theta), & \gamma<0.
  \end{cases}
\end{equation}
\item If the entries of $R$ lie in $\mathbb{Q}(i)$, the entries of $V$ are
  rational and $\theta$ is rational, then $\widetilde R$, $B$ and $E$ have
  rational entries, $\gamma$ is rational, the hypothesis on $\theta$ is a
  comparison of rationals, and the right-hand side of
  \eqref{eq:least-eigenvalue-bound} is a rational number.
\item Applied to $-R$, (ii) bounds the largest eigenvalue of $R$, which is
  $-\lmin(-R)$, from above.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}
\claimmeta{\metalabel{Used by}\mref{Cor.}{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:certified-evaluation}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:verified-feasible-side}, \extref{../receiver/contract.pdf}{receiver/req:rigorous-weight}, \extref{../receiver/contract.pdf}{receiver/thm:exact-and-evaluated}
\metasep newly derived
\metasep implemented
\metasep \metalabel{Code}\coderef{https://github.com/fraunhofersg/certiqs-key/blob/v0.1.0/src/certiqs_key/foundations/dyadic.py}{certiqs_key.foundations.dyadic:least_eigenvalue_bound}}

\begin{proof}
\emph{(i).} Write $A\coloneqq\mathrm{Re}\,R$ and $C\coloneqq\mathrm{Im}\,R$.
Since $R$ is Hermitian, $\overline{R_{li}}=R_{il}$ for all $i,l$, so
$A_{li}=A_{il}$ and $C_{li}=-C_{il}$: $A$ is symmetric and $C$ is
antisymmetric. Hence
$\widetilde R^{\transpose}=\begin{pmatrix}A^{\transpose}&C^{\transpose}\\
-C^{\transpose}&A^{\transpose}\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}A&-C\\C&A\end{pmatrix}=\widetilde R$. For
$x=\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, with
$a,b\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$, put $u\coloneqq a+ib\in\mathbb{C}^{n}$. Then
$Ru=(Aa-Cb)+i(Ca+Ab)$ and
\begin{equation*}
  u^{\dagger}Ru
  =a^{\transpose}(Aa-Cb)+b^{\transpose}(Ca+Ab)
  +i\big(a^{\transpose}(Ca+Ab)-b^{\transpose}(Aa-Cb)\big).
\end{equation*}
The number $u^{\dagger}Ru$ is real, $R$ being Hermitian, so it equals its
real part
$a^{\transpose}Aa-a^{\transpose}Cb+b^{\transpose}Ca+b^{\transpose}Ab$, which
is $x^{\transpose}\widetilde Rx$ written out by blocks; and
$u^{\dagger}u=a^{\transpose}a+b^{\transpose}b=x^{\transpose}x$. The map
$x\mapsto u$ is a bijection of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ onto $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ that
sends $0$ to $0$, so the set of Rayleigh quotients
$u^{\dagger}Ru/u^{\dagger}u$, $u\ne0$, equals the set of
$x^{\transpose}\widetilde Rx/x^{\transpose}x$, $x\ne0$. By the spectral
theorem the least eigenvalue of a Hermitian matrix is the minimum of its
Rayleigh quotient over non-zero complex vectors, and the least eigenvalue of
a real symmetric matrix, which has a real orthonormal eigenbasis, is the
minimum of its Rayleigh quotient over non-zero real vectors. So
$\lmin(\widetilde R)=\lmin(R)$.

\emph{(ii), the Gram matrix.} For $y\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}$,
$\|Vy\|^{2}=y^{\transpose}V^{\transpose}Vy=\|y\|^{2}+y^{\transpose}Ey$.
By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality applied to each row of $E$,
$\|Ey\|^{2}=\sum_i\big(\sum_lE_{il}y_l\big)^{2}
\le\sum_i\sum_lE_{il}^{2}\,\|y\|^{2}\le\theta^{2}\|y\|^{2}$, and again by
the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality $|y^{\transpose}Ey|\le\|y\|\,\|Ey\|
\le\theta\|y\|^{2}$. Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gram-sandwich}
  (1-\theta)\|y\|^{2}\;\le\;\|Vy\|^{2}\;\le\;(1+\theta)\|y\|^{2}
  \qquad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}.
\end{equation}
As $\theta<1$, $Vy=0$ forces $y=0$, so the square matrix $V$ is injective
and hence invertible.

\emph{(ii), Gershgorin's bound on the quadratic form.} $B$ is real symmetric,
$B^{\transpose}=V^{\transpose}\widetilde R^{\transpose}V=B$ by (i). For
$y\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, using $|y_iy_l|\le\tfrac12(y_i^{2}+y_l^{2})$, so that
$B_{il}y_iy_l\ge-|B_{il}|\,|y_iy_l|\ge-\tfrac12|B_{il}|(y_i^{2}+y_l^{2})$
whatever the signs of $B_{il}$, $y_i$ and $y_l$, and
$|B_{il}|=|B_{li}|$,
\begin{equation*}
  y^{\transpose}By=\sum_iB_{ii}y_i^{2}+\sum_{i\ne l}B_{il}y_iy_l
  \ge\sum_iB_{ii}y_i^{2}-\tfrac12\sum_{i\ne l}|B_{il}|\big(y_i^{2}+y_l^{2}\big)
  =\sum_iy_i^{2}\Big(B_{ii}-\sum_{l\ne i}|B_{il}|\Big)
  \ge\gamma\,\|y\|^{2},
\end{equation*}
the equality because the two halves of the double sum are equal after the
indices are exchanged, $|B_{il}|$ being symmetric in $i$ and $l$.

\emph{(ii), the bound.} Let $x\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, $x\ne0$, and put
$y\coloneqq V^{-1}x\ne0$. Then
$x^{\transpose}\widetilde Rx=y^{\transpose}V^{\transpose}\widetilde RVy
=y^{\transpose}By\ge\gamma\|y\|^{2}$, and $\|x\|^{2}=\|Vy\|^{2}$ lies
between $(1-\theta)\|y\|^{2}$ and $(1+\theta)\|y\|^{2}$ by
\eqref{eq:gram-sandwich}. If $\gamma\ge0$, then
$\|y\|^{2}\ge\|x\|^{2}/(1+\theta)$ gives
$\gamma\|y\|^{2}\ge\gamma\|x\|^{2}/(1+\theta)$. If $\gamma<0$, then
$\|y\|^{2}\le\|x\|^{2}/(1-\theta)$, the denominator being positive, gives
$\gamma\|y\|^{2}\ge\gamma\|x\|^{2}/(1-\theta)$. In either case the Rayleigh
quotient $x^{\transpose}\widetilde Rx/x^{\transpose}x$ is at least the
right-hand side of \eqref{eq:least-eigenvalue-bound}. Since $x$ was
arbitrary, so is $\lmin(\widetilde R)$, the minimum of that quotient, and
$\lmin(\widetilde R)=\lmin(R)$ by (i).

\emph{(iii).} The real and imaginary parts of an element of
$\mathbb{Q}(i)$ are rational, so $\widetilde R$ is rational; $B$ and $E$
are sums of products of rationals; $|B_{il}|$, the sums and the minimum
defining $\gamma$ are rational; $\sum_{i,l}E_{il}^{2}\le\theta^{2}$,
$0\le\theta$ and $\theta<1$ compare rationals; and $1\pm\theta>0$ is
rational, so the quotient is.

\emph{(iv).} $-R$ is Hermitian, its real embedding is $-\widetilde R$, and
its eigenvalues are those of $R$ with the sign reversed, so the largest
eigenvalue of $R$ is $-\lmin(-R)$, and a lower bound on $\lmin(-R)$ from
(ii) gives an upper bound on it.
\end{proof}

% claim foundations/cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure
\claimsummary{foundations/cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}{A Hermitian matrix within \ensuremath{\rho} of a Hermitian M in Frobenius norm has its spectrum within \ensuremath{\rho} of M's extreme eigenvalues. An entrywise enclosure whose exactly zero rows are dropped and whose rest certifies a positive least eigenvalue fixes the rank and support of every Hermitian matrix it contains.}
\claimbookmark{foundations/cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}{Corollary}{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}{Least eigenvalue and rank over an enclosure}
\claimleadin{%
Lemma~\ref{lem:least-eigenvalue-bound} bounds the least eigenvalue of a
matrix known exactly. An evaluation in ball arithmetic knows a matrix only
through an enclosure: part~(i) carries the bound across a ball in Frobenius
norm around an exact matrix, which is Weyl's inequality at the two ends of the
spectrum, and part~(ii) reads an \termref{term-entrywise-enclosure}{entrywise enclosure} as such a ball.
Parts~(iii) and~(iv) decide the rank of every matrix an enclosure contains at
once: the rows the enclosure fixes at zero are removed, and the rest must be
positive definite throughout the enclosure. Where the rest is not shown to be,
and in particular where its centre vanishes, the enclosure decides no rank,
and the corollary claims none.
}
\begin{technicalclaim}
\begin{corollary}[Least eigenvalue and rank over an enclosure]\label{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}
Let $n\ge1$, and for a complex $n\times n$ matrix $X$ write
$\|X\|_{\mathrm F}\coloneqq\big(\sum_{i,l}|X_{il}|^{2}\big)^{1/2}$ and
$\opn{X}\coloneqq\max\{\|Xx\|:x\in\mathbb{C}^{n},\ \|x\|=1\}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item \emph{(A ball in Frobenius norm.)} Let $R$ and $M$ be Hermitian
  $n\times n$ matrices and $\rho\ge0$ with $\|R-M\|_{\mathrm F}\le\rho$. Then
  $\opn{R-M}\le\|R-M\|_{\mathrm F}$, and
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:frobenius-ball}
    \lmin(R)\;\ge\;\lmin(M)-\rho,
    \qquad
    \lmax(R)\;\le\;\lmax(M)+\rho,
  \end{equation}
  so that every eigenvalue of $R$ lies in
  $[\lmin(M)-\rho,\lmax(M)+\rho]$. In particular $\lmin(R)\ge\ell-\rho$ for
  every lower bound $\ell$ on $\lmin(M)$, the right-hand side of
  \eqref{eq:least-eigenvalue-bound} for $M$ among them.
\item \emph{(An entrywise enclosure.)} If $(C,r)$ is an entrywise enclosure of
  $R$ (Definition~\ref{def:exact-reference}) and $\rho$ is a rational with
  $\rho\ge0$ and $\rho^{2}\ge\sum_{i,l}r_{il}^{2}$, then
  $\|R-C\|_{\mathrm F}\le\rho$ and (i) applies with $M=C$; whether $\rho$
  qualifies is a comparison of rationals.
\item \emph{(A factor form fixes the rank.)} Let $1\le k\le n$, let $E$ be a
  $k\times n$ matrix of rank $k$ and $\widetilde X$ a positive definite
  $k\times k$ matrix, and put $X\coloneqq E^{\dagger}\widetilde XE$. Then
  $X\succeq0$, $\operatorname{ran}X=\operatorname{ran}E^{\dagger}$ and
  $\operatorname{rank}X=k$.
\item \emph{(The rank over an entrywise enclosure.)} Let $C$ be a Hermitian
  $n\times n$ matrix with entries in $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ and $r_{il}=r_{li}\ge0$
  rationals, and say that $(C,r)$ \emph{contains} a Hermitian $X$ when
  $|X_{il}-C_{il}|\le r_{il}$ for all $i,l$. Let
  $Z\coloneqq\{i:C_{il}=0\text{ and }r_{il}=0\text{ for every }l\}$, the rows
  the pair fixes at zero, let $K$ be its complement in $\{1,\dots,n\}$ and
  $k\coloneqq|K|$. If $k=0$, the zero matrix is the only Hermitian matrix
  $(C,r)$ contains. If $k\ge1$, let $E$ be the $k\times n$ matrix whose rows
  are the transposed standard basis vectors $e_i^{\transpose}$, $i\in K$, in
  increasing order; then every Hermitian $X$ that $(C,r)$ contains satisfies
  $X=E^{\dagger}(EXE^{\dagger})E$. If moreover $\ell_K\le\lmin(ECE^{\dagger})$
  and a rational $\rho_K\ge0$ with $\rho_K^{2}\ge\sum_{i,l\in K}r_{il}^{2}$
  satisfy $\ell_K-\rho_K>0$, then for every Hermitian $X$ that $(C,r)$
  contains, $EXE^{\dagger}\succ0$, and so, by (iii), $X\succeq0$,
  $\operatorname{ran}X=\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in K\}$ and
  $\operatorname{rank}X=k$: the factor $E$, the support and the rank are the
  same for every such $X$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
\end{technicalclaim}
\claimmeta{\metalabel{Uses}\mref{Def.}{def:exact-reference}, \mref{Lem.}{lem:least-eigenvalue-bound}
\metasep \metalabel{Used by}\mref{Cor.}{cor:rank-over-factor-enclosure}, \mref{Lem.}{lem:matrix-function-perturbation}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:certified-bracket}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:certified-bracket-enclosed}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/rem:certified-scope}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:certified-evaluation}, \extref{../receiver/contract.pdf}{receiver/req:rigorous-weight}, \extref{../receiver/contract.pdf}{receiver/thm:exact-and-evaluated}
\metasep newly derived
\metasep implemented
\metasep \metalabel{Code}\coderef{https://github.com/fraunhofersg/certiqs-key/blob/v0.1.0/src/certiqs_key/foundations/dyadic.py}{certiqs_key.foundations.dyadic:enclosure_eigenvalue_bounds}}

\begin{proof}
\emph{(i).} Let $A$ be a complex $n\times n$ matrix and $x$ a unit vector.
By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality applied to each row,
$\|Ax\|^{2}=\sum_i\big|\sum_lA_{il}x_l\big|^{2}
\le\sum_i\big(\sum_l|A_{il}|^{2}\big)\|x\|^{2}=\|A\|_{\mathrm F}^{2}$, so
$\opn{A}\le\|A\|_{\mathrm F}$, and $|x^{\dagger}Ax|\le\|x\|\,\|Ax\|
\le\|A\|_{\mathrm F}$. With $A=R-M$, for every unit $x$,
$x^{\dagger}Rx=x^{\dagger}Mx+x^{\dagger}(R-M)x$ lies between
$x^{\dagger}Mx-\rho$ and $x^{\dagger}Mx+\rho$, hence between
$\lmin(M)-\rho$ and $\lmax(M)+\rho$, since the Rayleigh quotient of the
Hermitian $M$ lies between its extreme eigenvalues. The least and the
largest eigenvalue of the Hermitian $R$ are the minimum and the maximum of
$x^{\dagger}Rx$ over unit $x$, which gives \eqref{eq:frobenius-ball}, and
every eigenvalue of $R$ lies between them. The last sentence follows from
$\lmin(M)\ge\ell$.

\emph{(ii).} By \eqref{eq:entrywise-enclosure},
$\|R-C\|_{\mathrm F}^{2}=\sum_{i,l}|R_{il}-C_{il}|^{2}\le\sum_{i,l}r_{il}^{2}
\le\rho^{2}$, and $C$ is Hermitian by Definition~\ref{def:exact-reference}.
The sum of the squares of finitely many rationals is rational.

\emph{(iii).} For every $x$,
$x^{\dagger}Xx=(Ex)^{\dagger}\widetilde X(Ex)\ge0$, so $X\succeq0$, and
$x^{\dagger}Xx=0$ exactly when $Ex=0$, $\widetilde X$ being positive
definite. For a positive semidefinite $X$, $Xx=0$ exactly when
$x^{\dagger}Xx=0$, since $x^{\dagger}Xx=\|X^{1/2}x\|^{2}$ and
$Xx=X^{1/2}(X^{1/2}x)$. So $\ker X=\ker E$, and, $X$ being Hermitian,
$\operatorname{ran}X=(\ker X)^{\perp}=(\ker E)^{\perp}
=\operatorname{ran}E^{\dagger}$, whose dimension is
$\operatorname{rank}E=k$.

\emph{(iv).} Let $X$ be Hermitian and contained in $(C,r)$. For $i\in Z$ and
every $l$, $|X_{il}|=|X_{il}-C_{il}|\le r_{il}=0$, so row $i$ of $X$
vanishes, and so does column $i$, $X$ being Hermitian. If $k=0$, every row
vanishes and $X=0$, which $(C,r)$ contains. If $k\ge1$, $E^{\dagger}E$ is the
diagonal matrix with entry $1$ at the indices of $K$ and $0$ at those of $Z$,
so $E^{\dagger}EXE^{\dagger}E$ is $X$ with the rows and columns of $Z$ set
to zero, which is $X$. The matrix $EXE^{\dagger}$ is the principal
submatrix of $X$ on $K$, Hermitian, and $|(EXE^{\dagger})_{il}
-(ECE^{\dagger})_{il}|\le r_{il}$ for $i,l\in K$, so
$\|EXE^{\dagger}-ECE^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm F}\le\rho_K$ as in (ii), with
$ECE^{\dagger}$ Hermitian. By (i),
$\lmin(EXE^{\dagger})\ge\ell_K-\rho_K>0$, so $EXE^{\dagger}$ is positive
definite, and (iii) applies with $\widetilde X=EXE^{\dagger}$; $E$ has rank
$k$, its rows being distinct standard basis vectors, and
$\operatorname{ran}E^{\dagger}=\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in K\}$. Neither
$E$ nor $k$ depends on $X$.
\end{proof}

% claim foundations/cor:rank-over-factor-enclosure
\claimsummary{foundations/cor:rank-over-factor-enclosure}{A factor enclosure with no column holds only the zero matrix. One whose Gram matrix L*L has a positive floor over its box fixes, at every member, the rank, its number of columns, and the support, the span of that member's columns.}
\claimbookmark{foundations/cor:rank-over-factor-enclosure}{Corollary}{cor:rank-over-factor-enclosure}{Rank over a factor enclosure}
\claimleadin{%
Corollary~\ref{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}\,(iv) fixes the rank of
the matrices an entrywise enclosure contains where they are positive definite
on the rows it does not fix at zero. A \termref{term-factor-enclosure}{factor enclosure} fixes it where
the columns of its factors are linearly independent throughout the box, which
a positive floor under their Gram matrix shows: every member then has as many
independent columns as the triple has, and its support is the span of its own
columns. The support moves with the member, its dimension does not, and each
member has a factor form whose factor lies in a box and whose core is the same
exact matrix for all. Part~(iii) gives one floor that is a comparison of
rationals.
}
\begin{technicalclaim}
\begin{corollary}[Rank over a factor enclosure]\label{cor:rank-over-factor-enclosure}
Let $(L_c,t,W)$ be a triple of a \termref{term-matrix-box}{matrix box} $(L_c,t)$ of complex
$d\times k$ matrices and a diagonal $k\times k$ matrix $W$ with positive
rational diagonal entries, as in Definition~\ref{def:factor-enclosure}, and
call a matrix $L$ that the box contains a \emph{factor} and $LWL^{\dagger}$ a
\emph{member}.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item \emph{(No column.)} If $k=0$, every member is the zero $d\times d$
  matrix.
\item \emph{(A Gram floor fixes the rank.)} Let $k\ge1$, let $G$ be a
  Hermitian $k\times k$ matrix and $\rho\ge0$ with
  $\|L^{\dagger}L-G\|_{\mathrm F}\le\rho$ for every factor $L$, the Frobenius
  norm of Corollary~\ref{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}, and let
  $\ell\le\lmin(G)$ with $\ell-\rho>0$. Then for every factor $L$,
  $L^{\dagger}L\succ0$, so that $k\le d$ and $\operatorname{rank}L=k$; and the
  member $X\coloneqq LWL^{\dagger}$ satisfies $X=E^{\dagger}WE$ with
  $E\coloneqq L^{\dagger}$ a $k\times d$ matrix of rank $k$, $X\succeq0$,
  $\operatorname{ran}X=\operatorname{ran}L$, the span of the columns of $L$,
  and $\operatorname{rank}X=k$; in particular $X\neq0$.
\item \emph{(One such floor.)} Let $k\ge1$, put
  $a_{im}\coloneqq|\operatorname{Re}(L_c)_{im}|+|\operatorname{Im}(L_c)_{im}|$
  and
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:gram-radius}
    s_{ml}\;\coloneqq\;\sum_{i=1}^{d}\big(a_{im}t_{il}+t_{im}a_{il}
    +t_{im}t_{il}\big)\qquad(1\le m,l\le k),
  \end{equation}
  rationals. Then $G\coloneqq L_c^{\dagger}L_c$ is Hermitian with entries in
  $\mathbb{Q}(i)$, and every rational $\rho\ge0$ with
  $\rho^{2}\ge\sum_{m,l}s_{ml}^{2}$ satisfies
  $\|L^{\dagger}L-G\|_{\mathrm F}\le\rho$ for every factor $L$; whether $\rho$
  qualifies, and whether $\ell-\rho>0$ for a rational $\ell$, is a comparison
  of rationals.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
\end{technicalclaim}
\claimmeta{\metalabel{Uses}\mref{Def.}{def:factor-enclosure}, \mref{Cor.}{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}
\metasep \metalabel{Used by}\extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:certified-bracket-enclosed}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/rem:certified-scope}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:certified-evaluation}, \extref{../receiver/contract.pdf}{receiver/detector-imperfections/req:dark-composed-reference}
\metasep newly derived
\metasep implemented
\metasep \metalabel{Code}\coderef{https://github.com/fraunhofersg/certiqs-key/blob/v0.1.0/src/certiqs_key/foundations/reference.py}{certiqs_key.foundations.reference:fixes_rank}}

\begin{proof}
\emph{(i).} For $k=0$ a factor $L$ is $d\times0$ and $W$ is $0\times0$, so
every entry $(LWL^{\dagger})_{il}=\sum_{m=1}^{k}L_{im}W_{mm}\overline{L_{lm}}$
is an empty sum, $0$.

\emph{(ii).} Let $L$ be a factor. $L^{\dagger}L$ is a Hermitian $k\times k$
matrix, and Corollary~\ref{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}\,(i) with
$R\coloneqq L^{\dagger}L$ and $M\coloneqq G$ gives
$\lmin(L^{\dagger}L)\ge\lmin(G)-\rho\ge\ell-\rho>0$. So for $y\ne0$,
$\|Ly\|^{2}=y^{\dagger}L^{\dagger}Ly>0$: $L$ is injective, its rank is $k$,
and $k\le d$, the rank of a $d\times k$ matrix being at most $d$. The adjoint
$E=L^{\dagger}$ has the same rank $k$, and $E^{\dagger}WE=LWL^{\dagger}=X$
with $W$ positive definite, its diagonal entries being positive.
Corollary~\ref{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}\,(iii), with $E$ and
$\widetilde X\coloneqq W$, gives $X\succeq0$,
$\operatorname{ran}X=\operatorname{ran}E^{\dagger}=\operatorname{ran}L$ and
$\operatorname{rank}X=k\ge1$, so $X\ne0$.

\emph{(iii).} The entries $(L_c^{\dagger}L_c)_{ml}=\sum_i
\overline{(L_c)_{im}}(L_c)_{il}$ are sums of products of Gaussian rationals,
so they lie in $\mathbb{Q}(i)$, and
$\overline{(L_c^{\dagger}L_c)_{lm}}=(L_c^{\dagger}L_c)_{ml}$. Let $L$ be a
factor and $\Delta\coloneqq L-L_c$, so $|\Delta_{im}|\le t_{im}$. Then
\begin{equation*}
  (L^{\dagger}L-L_c^{\dagger}L_c)_{ml}
  =\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Big(\overline{(L_c)_{im}}\,\Delta_{il}
  +\overline{\Delta_{im}}\,(L_c)_{il}+\overline{\Delta_{im}}\,\Delta_{il}\Big),
\end{equation*}
and $|(L_c)_{im}|\le a_{im}$, since $|x+iy|\le|x|+|y|$ for real $x,y$; by the
triangle inequality the modulus of the left-hand side is at most $s_{ml}$.
Hence $\|L^{\dagger}L-G\|_{\mathrm F}^{2}=\sum_{m,l}|(L^{\dagger}L-G)_{ml}|^{2}
\le\sum_{m,l}s_{ml}^{2}\le\rho^{2}$. The $a_{im}$ and $s_{ml}$ are sums and
products of rationals, and so is $\sum_{m,l}s_{ml}^{2}$.
\end{proof}

% claim foundations/lem:matrix-function-perturbation
\claimsummary{foundations/lem:matrix-function-perturbation}{On Hermitian matrices with spectra in an interval, a function with derivative bounded by L moves at most L times the perturbation in Frobenius norm, and the divided-difference map of x\textasciicircum{}p at most p(1\ensuremath{-}p)a\textasciicircum{}(p\ensuremath{-}2) times it above a floor a. Close arguments get a second-order bound.}
\claimbookmark{foundations/lem:matrix-function-perturbation}{Lemma}{lem:matrix-function-perturbation}{Perturbation bounds for matrix functions}
\claimleadin{%
The gradient of the pinched trace power is built from powers of positive
definite matrices and from the divided-difference map of $x\mapsto x^{p}$
(\xref{meat-core/lem:dk}, \xref{meat-core/thm:gradient}). An evaluation in
ball arithmetic has such a matrix only as an exactly unitary $U$ and an exact
diagonal $\Lambda$ with $U^{\dagger}NU=\Lambda+E$ and $E$ small; the lemma
says how far each quantity can move under $E$. Part~(i) bounds the values
and traces of a function, part~(ii) moves them through $U$, and part~(iii)
bounds the divided-difference map by an integral representation of
$x\mapsto x^{p}$, whose constant comes out exactly without being computed.
Part~(iv) encloses a divided difference of two close arguments without the
cancellation of the quotient.
}
\begin{technicalclaim}
\begin{lemma}[Perturbation bounds for matrix functions]\label{lem:matrix-function-perturbation}
Let $n\ge1$, write $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm F}$ and $\opn{\cdot}$ as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}, and let $P$, $Q$ be
Hermitian $n\times n$ matrices. For a real function $f$ defined on a set
containing the spectrum of $P$, with $P=\sum_a\mu_a\Pi_a$ its spectral
decomposition into distinct eigenvalues $\mu_a$ and spectral projectors
$\Pi_a$, put $f(P)\coloneqq\sum_af(\mu_a)\Pi_a$. For real $x\ne y$ put
$f^{[1]}(x,y)\coloneqq(f(x)-f(y))/(x-y)$, and $f^{[1]}(x,x)\coloneqq f'(x)$
where $f$ is differentiable at $x$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item \emph{(Values and traces.)} Let $I$ be an interval containing the
  spectra of $P$ and $Q$, let $f$ be continuous on $I$ and differentiable in
  its interior, and let $|f'|\le L$ there. Then
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:mf-lipschitz}
    \|f(P)-f(Q)\|_{\mathrm F}\le L\,\|P-Q\|_{\mathrm F},
    \qquad
    \big|\tr f(P)-\tr f(Q)\big|\le\sqrt n\,L\,\|P-Q\|_{\mathrm F},
  \end{equation}
  and every entry of $f(P)-f(Q)$ has modulus at most
  $L\,\|P-Q\|_{\mathrm F}$. For $f(x)=x^{s}$ on $I=[a,b]$ with $0<a\le b$,
  one may take $L=s\,a^{s-1}$ if $0<s\le1$ and $L=s\,b^{s-1}$ if $s\ge1$.
\item \emph{(Unitary covariance.)} For every unitary $U$,
  $f(UPU^{\dagger})=Uf(P)U^{\dagger}$, and
  $\|UXU^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm F}=\|X\|_{\mathrm F}$ for every $X$.
\item \emph{(The divided-difference map of a power.)} Let $0<p<1$ and
  $f(x)=x^{p}$ on $(0,\infty)$. For a positive definite $P=\sum_a\mu_a\Pi_a$
  and every complex $n\times n$ matrix $H$ put
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:dd-map}
    \mathrm{D}_P[H]\coloneqq\sum_{a,b}f^{[1]}(\mu_a,\mu_b)\,\Pi_aH\Pi_b .
  \end{equation}
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
  \item $J_p\coloneqq\int_0^{\infty}u^{p-1}(1+u)^{-1}\,\mathrm du$ is finite
    and positive, and with $c_p\coloneqq1/J_p$,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:dd-integral}
      \mathrm{D}_P[H]=c_p\int_0^{\infty}t^{p}\,(P+t)^{-1}H(P+t)^{-1}\,\mathrm dt,
    \end{equation}
    the integral taken entry by entry, each entry's integrand absolutely
    integrable.
  \item If $Q$ is positive definite as well and $0<a\le\min\{\lmin(P),
    \lmin(Q)\}$, then
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:dd-lipschitz}
      \big\|\mathrm{D}_P[H]-\mathrm{D}_Q[H]\big\|_{\mathrm F}
      \;\le\;p(1-p)\,a^{p-2}\,\opn{P-Q}\,\|H\|_{\mathrm F}
      \;\le\;p(1-p)\,a^{p-2}\,\|P-Q\|_{\mathrm F}\,\|H\|_{\mathrm F}.
    \end{equation}
  \item For every unitary $U$,
    $\mathrm{D}_{UPU^{\dagger}}[H]=U\,\mathrm{D}_P[U^{\dagger}HU]\,U^{\dagger}$;
    and if $P=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\dots,d_n)$, the $d_k>0$ not
    necessarily distinct, then
    $\mathrm{D}_P[H]_{kl}=f^{[1]}(d_k,d_l)\,H_{kl}$ for all $k,l$.
  \end{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Close arguments.)} Let $y\le x$, let $f$ be three times
  continuously differentiable on an open interval containing $[y,x]$, and put
  $m\coloneqq(x+y)/2$ and $d\coloneqq x-y$. Then
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:dd-close}
    \big|f^{[1]}(x,y)-f'(m)\big|\;\le\;\frac{d^{2}}{24}\,
    \max_{\xi\in[y,x]}|f'''(\xi)| .
  \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}
\end{technicalclaim}
\claimmeta{\metalabel{Uses}\mref{Cor.}{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}
\metasep \metalabel{Used by}\extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:certified-evaluation}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/lem:kraus-freedom}
\metasep newly derived
\metasep implemented
\metasep \metalabel{Code}\coderef{https://github.com/fraunhofersg/certiqs-key/blob/v0.1.0/src/certiqs_key/foundations/balls.py}{certiqs_key.foundations.balls:deriv_power}}

\begin{proof}
\emph{(i).} Let $\{u_i\}$ and $\{v_j\}$ be orthonormal eigenbases of $P$ and
$Q$, with $Pu_i=p_iu_i$ and $Qv_j=q_jv_j$, and let $U$ and $V$ be the unitary
matrices with these columns. For every matrix $A$, $U^{\dagger}AV$ has the
entries $u_i^{\dagger}Av_j$, and
$\|U^{\dagger}AV\|_{\mathrm F}^{2}=\tr[V^{\dagger}A^{\dagger}UU^{\dagger}AV]
=\tr[A^{\dagger}A]=\|A\|_{\mathrm F}^{2}$, so
$\|A\|_{\mathrm F}^{2}=\sum_{i,j}|u_i^{\dagger}Av_j|^{2}$. Since
$u_i^{\dagger}f(P)=f(p_i)u_i^{\dagger}$ and $f(Q)v_j=f(q_j)v_j$,
\begin{equation*}
  u_i^{\dagger}\big(f(P)-f(Q)\big)v_j=\big(f(p_i)-f(q_j)\big)u_i^{\dagger}v_j,
  \qquad
  u_i^{\dagger}(P-Q)v_j=(p_i-q_j)\,u_i^{\dagger}v_j .
\end{equation*}
Both $p_i$ and $q_j$ lie in the interval $I$, and so does the segment between
them; if $p_i\ne q_j$, the mean value theorem on that segment gives
$|f(p_i)-f(q_j)|\le L|p_i-q_j|$, and if $p_i=q_j$ both sides vanish. Hence
$|u_i^{\dagger}(f(P)-f(Q))v_j|\le L|u_i^{\dagger}(P-Q)v_j|$ for all $i,j$,
and summing the squares gives the first inequality of
\eqref{eq:mf-lipschitz}. Every entry of a matrix $A$ has modulus at most
$\|A\|_{\mathrm F}$, and
$|\tr A|=|\sum_kA_{kk}|\le\sqrt n\,(\sum_k|A_{kk}|^{2})^{1/2}
\le\sqrt n\,\|A\|_{\mathrm F}$ by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, which with
$A=f(P)-f(Q)$ gives the rest. For $f(x)=x^{s}$, $f'(x)=s\,x^{s-1}$, which is
non-increasing on $[a,b]$ if $s\le1$ and non-decreasing if $s\ge1$, so its
maximum there is $s\,a^{s-1}$, respectively $s\,b^{s-1}$.

\emph{(ii).} The matrices $U\Pi_aU^{\dagger}$ are orthogonal projectors,
mutually orthogonal and summing to the identity, and
$UPU^{\dagger}=\sum_a\mu_aU\Pi_aU^{\dagger}$, so they are the spectral
projectors of $UPU^{\dagger}$ and
$f(UPU^{\dagger})=\sum_af(\mu_a)U\Pi_aU^{\dagger}=Uf(P)U^{\dagger}$. And
$\|UXU^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm F}^{2}=\tr[UX^{\dagger}U^{\dagger}UXU^{\dagger}]
=\tr[X^{\dagger}X]$.

\emph{(iii)(a), Step 1 (the constant).} The integrand of $J_p$ is positive
and continuous on $(0,\infty)$, at most $u^{p-1}$ on $(0,1]$, integrable
there since $p>0$, and at most $u^{p-2}$ on $[1,\infty)$, integrable there
since $p<1$; so $0<J_p<\infty$. For $x>0$ the substitution $t=xu$ gives
\begin{equation*}
  \int_0^{\infty}t^{p-1}\frac{x}{x+t}\,\mathrm dt
  =\int_0^{\infty}x^{p-1}u^{p-1}\frac{x}{x(1+u)}\,x\,\mathrm du
  =x^{p}J_p,
  \qquad\text{that is,}\qquad
  x^{p}=c_p\int_0^{\infty}t^{p-1}\frac{x}{x+t}\,\mathrm dt .
\end{equation*}

\emph{Step 2 (two integrals).} Integration by parts on $[\varepsilon,R]$,
$0<\varepsilon<R$, gives
\begin{gather*}
  \int_{\varepsilon}^{R}\frac{u^{p-1}}{1+u}\,\mathrm du
  =\Big[\frac{u^{p}}{p(1+u)}\Big]_{\varepsilon}^{R}
  +\frac1p\int_{\varepsilon}^{R}\frac{u^{p}}{(1+u)^{2}}\,\mathrm du,\\
  \int_{\varepsilon}^{R}\frac{u^{p}}{(1+u)^{3}}\,\mathrm du
  =\Big[-\frac{u^{p}}{2(1+u)^{2}}\Big]_{\varepsilon}^{R}
  +\frac p2\int_{\varepsilon}^{R}\frac{u^{p-1}}{(1+u)^{2}}\,\mathrm du .
\end{gather*}
The boundary terms tend to $0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$ and $R\to\infty$, since
$0<p<1$, and the integrals on the right converge, their integrands being
bounded by $u^{p}$ or $u^{p-1}$ near $0$ and by $u^{p-2}$ or $u^{p-3}$ at
infinity. So $\int_0^{\infty}u^{p}(1+u)^{-2}\,\mathrm du=pJ_p$. Since
$u^{p-1}(1+u)^{-2}=u^{p-1}(1+u)^{-1}-u^{p}(1+u)^{-2}$, the numerator of the
difference being $u^{p-1}\big((1+u)-u\big)$,
$\int_0^{\infty}u^{p-1}(1+u)^{-2}\,\mathrm du=J_p-pJ_p=(1-p)J_p$, and so
\begin{equation*}
  \int_0^{\infty}\frac{u^{p}}{(1+u)^{2}}\,\mathrm du=p\,J_p,
  \qquad
  \int_0^{\infty}\frac{u^{p}}{(1+u)^{3}}\,\mathrm du
  =\frac{p(1-p)}{2}\,J_p .
\end{equation*}

\emph{Step 3 (divided differences).} Let $x,y>0$. If $x\ne y$, then
$\frac{x}{x+t}-\frac{y}{y+t}=\frac{t(x-y)}{(x+t)(y+t)}$, and the two
integrals of Step~1 converge separately, so
$f^{[1]}(x,y)=c_p\int_0^{\infty}t^{p}\,(x+t)^{-1}(y+t)^{-1}\,\mathrm dt$.
If $x=y$, the substitution $t=xu$ and Step~2 give
$c_p\int_0^{\infty}t^{p}(x+t)^{-2}\,\mathrm dt
=c_p\,x^{p-1}\int_0^{\infty}u^{p}(1+u)^{-2}\,\mathrm du=p\,x^{p-1}=f'(x)$.
So in either case
\begin{equation*}
  f^{[1]}(x,y)=c_p\int_0^{\infty}\frac{t^{p}}{(x+t)(y+t)}\,\mathrm dt .
\end{equation*}

\emph{Step 4 (the map).} For $t\ge0$, $P+t$ is positive definite with
$(P+t)^{-1}=\sum_a(\mu_a+t)^{-1}\Pi_a$, so
$t^{p}(P+t)^{-1}H(P+t)^{-1}=\sum_{a,b}t^{p}(\mu_a+t)^{-1}(\mu_b+t)^{-1}
\Pi_aH\Pi_b$, a finite sum whose scalar coefficients are integrable by
Step~3. Integrating term by term and using Step~3 gives
\eqref{eq:dd-integral}.

\emph{(iii)(b).} Put $A_t\coloneqq(P+t)^{-1}$ and $B_t\coloneqq(Q+t)^{-1}$
for $t\ge0$. The eigenvalues of $A_t$ are $(\mu+t)^{-1}$ for the eigenvalues
$\mu\ge a$ of $P$, so $\opn{A_t}\le(a+t)^{-1}$, and likewise
$\opn{B_t}\le(a+t)^{-1}$. From
$A_t-B_t=A_t\big((Q+t)-(P+t)\big)B_t=A_t(Q-P)B_t$ and the
submultiplicativity of the operator norm,
$\opn{A_t-B_t}\le\opn{P-Q}(a+t)^{-2}$. For matrices $X$, $Y$, $W$,
$\|XYW\|_{\mathrm F}\le\opn{X}\,\|Y\|_{\mathrm F}\,\opn{W}$: column by
column, $\|XY\|_{\mathrm F}^{2}=\sum_l\|Xy_l\|^{2}\le\opn{X}^{2}
\|Y\|_{\mathrm F}^{2}$ for the columns $y_l$ of $Y$, and
$\|YW\|_{\mathrm F}=\|W^{\dagger}Y^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm F}
\le\opn{W}\,\|Y\|_{\mathrm F}$, the operator norm being invariant under the
adjoint. Since $A_tHA_t-B_tHB_t=(A_t-B_t)HA_t+B_tH(A_t-B_t)$,
\begin{equation*}
  \|A_tHA_t-B_tHB_t\|_{\mathrm F}\le2\,\opn{P-Q}\,\|H\|_{\mathrm F}\,(a+t)^{-3}.
\end{equation*}
By (a), $\mathrm{D}_P[H]-\mathrm{D}_Q[H]$ is the entrywise integral of
$\Phi(t)\coloneqq c_pt^{p}(A_tHA_t-B_tHB_t)$. For such an integral
$\Delta=\int_0^{\infty}\Phi(t)\,\mathrm dt$ with
$\int_0^{\infty}\|\Phi(t)\|_{\mathrm F}\,\mathrm dt<\infty$,
$\|\Delta\|_{\mathrm F}\le\int_0^{\infty}\|\Phi(t)\|_{\mathrm F}\,\mathrm dt$:
if $\Delta\ne0$, put $W\coloneqq\Delta/\|\Delta\|_{\mathrm F}$; then
$\|\Delta\|_{\mathrm F}=\operatorname{Re}\tr[W^{\dagger}\Delta]
=\int_0^{\infty}\operatorname{Re}\tr[W^{\dagger}\Phi(t)]\,\mathrm dt
\le\int_0^{\infty}\|\Phi(t)\|_{\mathrm F}\,\mathrm dt$, by linearity of the
entrywise integral and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for
$(X,Y)\mapsto\tr[X^{\dagger}Y]$. Hence, substituting $t=au$ and using
Step~2,
\begin{equation*}
  \|\mathrm{D}_P[H]-\mathrm{D}_Q[H]\|_{\mathrm F}
  \le2c_p\,\opn{P-Q}\,\|H\|_{\mathrm F}\int_0^{\infty}\frac{t^{p}}{(a+t)^{3}}\,\mathrm dt
  =2c_p\,a^{p-2}\,\frac{p(1-p)}{2}\,J_p\,\opn{P-Q}\,\|H\|_{\mathrm F},
\end{equation*}
which is the first inequality of \eqref{eq:dd-lipschitz}, as $c_pJ_p=1$. The
second is $\opn{P-Q}\le\|P-Q\|_{\mathrm F}$
(Corollary~\ref{cor:least-eigenvalue-over-enclosure}\,(i)).

\emph{(iii)(c).} By the argument of (ii), the spectral projectors of
$UPU^{\dagger}$ are the $U\Pi_aU^{\dagger}$, with the same eigenvalues, so
$\mathrm{D}_{UPU^{\dagger}}[H]=\sum_{a,b}f^{[1]}(\mu_a,\mu_b)\,
U\Pi_aU^{\dagger}HU\Pi_bU^{\dagger}=U\,\mathrm{D}_P[U^{\dagger}HU]\,U^{\dagger}$.
If $P$ is diagonal, $\Pi_a=\sum_{k:\,d_k=\mu_a}e_ke_k^{\dagger}$, so
$(\Pi_aH\Pi_b)_{kl}=H_{kl}$ when $d_k=\mu_a$ and $d_l=\mu_b$ and $0$
otherwise; summing over $a$ and $b$ leaves
$f^{[1]}(d_k,d_l)H_{kl}$ at $(k,l)$.

\emph{(iv).} If $d=0$, then $f^{[1]}(x,y)=f'(x)=f'(m)$. Otherwise put
$h\coloneqq d/2>0$. Taylor's theorem with the Lagrange remainder gives
$\xi_{+}\in(m,m+h)$ and $\xi_{-}\in(m-h,m)$ with
\begin{equation*}
  f(m\pm h)=f(m)\pm hf'(m)+\frac{h^{2}}2f''(m)\pm\frac{h^{3}}6f'''(\xi_{\pm}),
\end{equation*}
so $f(x)-f(y)=2hf'(m)+\frac{h^{3}}6\big(f'''(\xi_{+})+f'''(\xi_{-})\big)$.
Dividing by $d=2h$,
$f^{[1]}(x,y)-f'(m)=\frac{h^{2}}{12}\big(f'''(\xi_{+})+f'''(\xi_{-})\big)$,
whose modulus is at most $\frac{h^{2}}6\max_{[y,x]}|f'''|
=\frac{d^{2}}{24}\max_{[y,x]}|f'''|$.
\end{proof}

% claim foundations/def:tiers
\claimsummary{foundations/def:tiers}{A reported key rate carries one of three tiers: estimate, a returned point's objective, claiming no bound; first-order, a lower bound on the minimum under named hypotheses; or certified, such a bound with every step from the data exact or rigorously enclosed, no hypothesis about arithmetic.}
\claimbookmark{foundations/def:tiers}{Definition}{def:tiers}{The tiers of a reported key rate}
\claimleadin{%
In this repository the estimate is the objective value of
\xref{meat-core/lem:estimate}, and the first-order number is the linearisation
bound of the Frank--Wolfe solver, \xref{meat-core/frank-wolfe/thm:firstorder},
whose hypotheses include lower bounds on the two linear minima it reads. A
run evaluates that bound in binary64, so a first-order number rests, beside
the hypotheses of the theorem, on arithmetic that no claim bounds. The
certified number is the same bound formed again at a run's final points from
enclosures of the gradient
(\xref{meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:certified-bracket}), every step from the
declaration's data exact or carried out in an arithmetic that bounds its own
rounding, so that nothing is assumed of how it was computed.
}
\begin{definition}[The tiers of a reported key rate]\label{def:tiers}
A \termdef{term-tier}{tier} of a reported key-rate number is one
of the following three labels.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item \termdef{term-estimate}{estimate}: the
  number is the value of the objective at the point
  an optimiser returned. It is reported as an estimate of the minimum of the
  objective and is claimed as no bound.
\item \termdef{term-first-order}{first-order}: the number is a lower bound on the minimum of the
  objective, established by a claim under hypotheses that claim names.
\item \termdef{term-certified}{certified}: the number is a lower bound on the minimum
  of the objective of the declaration it is formed on, established by a claim
  under hypotheses that claim names, and every arithmetic step between that
  declaration's data and the number is exact or
  \termdef{term-rigorously-enclosed}{rigorously enclosed}: a
  computation is rigorously enclosed when each of its operations returns a
  set of numbers, such as an interval or a ball, that contains the exact
  result of the operation at every value the sets of its inputs contain, so
  that the set it ends with contains the exact value, at the exact data, of
  the quantity it computes. None of those hypotheses is an assumption about
  how a number was computed, that is, none is an assumption of the category
  numerical-trust.
\end{enumerate}
The tiers are ordered, estimate below first-order below certified, and a
tier is \emph{stronger} than the tiers below it. A certified number is a
first-order number as well. There is no other tier.
\end{definition}
\claimmeta{\metalabel{Used by}\mref{Req.}{req:snap-reference}, \mref{Req.}{req:exact-island}, \mref{Req.}{req:tiers}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/rem:certified-scope}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:certified-evaluation}, \extref{../meat-core/contract.pdf}{meat-core/req:unreachable-acceptance-set}, \extref{../receiver/contract.pdf}{receiver/detector-imperfections/req:dark-composed-reference}
\metasep newly derived
\metasep implemented
\metasep \metalabel{Code}\coderef{https://github.com/fraunhofersg/certiqs-key/blob/v0.1.0/src/certiqs_key/foundations/assurance.py}{certiqs_key.foundations.assurance:Assurance}}

\section{The snapped-measurement assumption}\label{group-foundations/ass:snapped-measurement}
\sectionintro{A moved block of a measurement snap is related to its model by no claim. Where the run reads it, because no reference reaches the evaluation, or the evaluation on the reference does not count, or the key length is formed from a number the run certified on the snapped family in its place, the analysis of the run is an analysis of the snapped family, the more so where a flagged last resort gave an element support the data deny. The one assumption of the module, \hyperlink{claim-foundations/ass:snapped-measurement}{Assumption~\ref*{ass:snapped-measurement}}, is the premise under which that analysis describes the device: on the blocks the record names, the device measures the snapped family as recorded, in place of the model there, and for a producer's snap of its own emission, what the run concludes from the emission holds of the snapped family. A block \termref{term-evaluated-off-its-snap}{evaluated off its snap} is never among them. A run with no such block, or a run that declares the strict option, does not rest on it.}

% claim foundations/ass:snapped-measurement
\claimsummary{foundations/ass:snapped-measurement}{On every moved block of a snap that the run does not evaluate off its snap, the device measures the snapped family; for a producer's snap of its own emission, what the run concludes from the emission holds of the snapped family there.}
\claimbookmark{foundations/ass:snapped-measurement}{Assumption}{ass:snapped-measurement}{The device measures the snapped family where the run reads the snap}
\claimleadin{%
A snap moves a measurement family onto a lattice
(Definition~\ref{def:snap}), and nothing established relates a moved block
to the model it replaced. A run that holds a \termref{term-reference}{reference} of the family
and evaluates the numbers its key length rests on with that reference in
place of the snap reads the snapped family only to find the points at which
it evaluates them; on such a block, \termref{term-evaluated-off-its-snap}{evaluated off its snap}, no premise
about the snap is needed, and this assumption does not cover it. Where the
run does read a moved block, because no reference reaches the evaluation, the
evaluation on the reference does not count, or the key length is formed from
a number certified on the snapped family in its place, the analysis of the
run is
there an analysis of the snapped family, a block whose data are an evaluation
of a model not known exactly on it included, even where the snap leaves that
evaluation as it stands. This assumption is the premise under which that
analysis describes the device. Where the snap had to give an element support
that the data deny, a block the record flags, the premise is stronger, since
the snapped family may treat as possible an outcome that the model treats as
impossible. On the blocks it covers it takes the place of the model as a
description of the device, so that the two are never asserted of the same
block; for a family that a producer snaps in its own emission, which is the
target of a reduction and not the measurement of a device, it is the premise
that what the run concludes from the emission holds of the snapped family. A
run none of whose blocks it covers does not invoke it.
}
\SetShortId{A-SNAP}
\begin{assumption}[The device measures the snapped family where the run reads the snap]\label{ass:snapped-measurement}
Let $F$ be a snap (Definition~\ref{def:snap}) of an operator family $D$ read
as a measurement, against a \termref{term-sector-map}{sector map} with blocks $s\in\mathsf{S}$
(Definition~\ref{def:sector-map}), over an alphabet $J$, with $D$ the data the
snap is made from: the data as an instance states them, or, where the
instance computes those data from a model of the family, that model, a
\termref{term-reference}{reference} of the family (Definition~\ref{def:exact-reference}), or a
producer's exact construction of what it emits
(Definition~\ref{def:declared-data}). Let $B\subseteq\mathsf{S}$ be the set of
blocks that the record of the run names as resting on this assumption: the
\termref{term-moved}{moved} blocks of $F$ (Definition~\ref{def:snap}), those on which the
record does not show, by an exact decision, that $F^{(s)}_j=D^{(s)}_j$ for
every $j\in J$, that are not \termref{term-evaluated-off-its-snap}{evaluated off its snap}
(Definition~\ref{def:evaluated-off-snap}). A \termref{term-kept}{kept} block and a block
evaluated off its snap do not belong to $B$. Every other moved block belongs
to $B$, whatever its cause; among them are the blocks on which the snap gives
an element support outside the \termref{term-structural-support}{structural support} of $D^{(s)}_j$
(Definition~\ref{def:snap}).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item Where $D$ is the data an instance states as the measurement of a
  device, the model it computes them from, or a reference of it, then on every block $s\in B$ the block on $s$
  of the measurement the device performs, read against the sector map, is
  the family $\{F^{(s)}_j\}_{j\in J}$ with the entries recorded for the snap.
  On such a block, any statement of another assumption of the run that a
  model describes that measurement is not asserted, and this clause holds in
  its place.
\item Where $D$ is a producer's exact construction of what it emits, every
  conclusion about the device that the claims of the run draw from the
  emitted family, under their hypothesis that it is the producer's exact
  construction, holds when the emitted family is $F^{(s)}$ on every block
  $s\in B$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{assumption}
\claimverification{The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.}
\claimreading{Applies only where the run record names blocks as resting on it, a premise about your device. The engine moves each measurement onto its numerical lattice. Where it holds a reference of your model, it computes the key rate on the model at the points the moved measurement found; where the reported rate was formed there, the blocks carrying the reference do not rest on this. On the named blocks, the key rate is computed as if the device performed the moved measurement. It may treat as possible an outcome your model treats as impossible, except in rows and columns the record states to be exactly zero; on a block flagged support\_not\_preserved, not even there. The engine cannot check this. The record names the cause and a fix: a model with a reference, a run that uses enclosed references, the reasons the reference's bound was not counted or certified, or your device's loss and dark counts.}
\claimmeta{\metalabel{Uses}\mref{Def.}{def:declared-data}, \mref{Def.}{def:sector-map}, \mref{Def.}{def:exact-reference}, \mref{Def.}{def:snap}, \mref{Def.}{def:evaluated-off-snap}
\metasep \metalabel{Category}receiver
\metasep \metalabel{Affects}secrecy, completeness
\metasep \metalabel{Assumed by}\mref{Req.}{req:snap-reference}, \mref{Req.}{req:exact-emission}, \extref{../reductions/contract.pdf}{reductions/cor:reference-companion}, \extref{../reductions/contract.pdf}{reductions/req:emission-record}, \extref{../reductions/contract.pdf}{reductions/thm:emit}
\metasep \metalabel{Machine key}\iface{snapped_measurement}
\metasep newly derived
\metasep accepted}
